To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pesticide residues of monocrotophos, acephate, cypermethrin and Neem seed extract are persistent and safe to T. indica, while the residues of dichlorvos and deltamethrin are shortlived and highly toxic.
the parasitoid T. indica is tolerant to most of the pesticides used against the mealybug P. lilacinus on acid lime.
the adult parasitoid of mealybug, T. indica was susceptible to 18 pesticides and the toxic effects of the insecticides on the adult parasitid was persistent upto 50 days.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an effective and environmentally safe pest management strategy on acid lime.
the effects of pesticides on a natural enemy of a major pest of citrus, and it is important for the development of integrated pest management programmes for this crop.
the development of a biological control program for the control of P. lilacinus on acid lime.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the pesticides in the field would not have any detrimental effects on the population of T. indica.

the pesticides used on the crop should be carefully selected and the timing of application should be such that the toxic residues of the pesticides are either not present on the crop or are below the level that would affect the parasitoids.
the insecticides tested were not found to be toxic to T. indicain the laboratory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of pesticides in the field should be avoided during peak parasitism period of T. indica, and that the pesticides with longer residual toxicity like monocrotophos, acephate and cypermethrin should be used in the field only when absolutely necessary.
T. indica can be used as a biological control agent for P. lilacinus on acid lime in the presence of monocrotophos.

, in general, the parasitoids of P. lilacinus are not affected by the pesticides used in the citrus groves and the pesticides which are toxic to the parasitic insects can be used in the citrus plantations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of pesticides in the management of mealybugs in acid lime should be done with care.
, the parasitoids are very important in pest management and they should be protected from the adverse effects of pesticides.
the use of pesticides in citrus orchards should be done with caution to avoid any adverse effect on the natural enemies.
